messages:
nina: Hey team, quick new-hire question: I enrolled myself in medical during onboarding but forgot to add my spouse as a dependent. Is there a special life event window for adding dependents or do I have to wait until open enrollment? cc @lisa :wave:
lisa: Hi Nina 97 welcome! If you missed adding your spouse during the initial new-hire window, you typically have 30 days from your hire date to add dependents as a qualifying life event (marriage counts). Did you add after onboarding or is the spouse already on your plan elsewhere?
nina: We got married last month but I only marked "self" in the portal. My hire date was 2026-06-02 and today is 2026-06-10. I can upload the marriage certificate. What's the exact process?
benefits-bot: Enrollment note: New-hire life event window = 30 days from hire date. To add a dependent, submit the dependent enrollment form and required documentation (marriage certificate or marriage affidavit) via the benefits portal. Link: https://redwood.intranet/benefits/dependent-enroll :link:
lisa: Correct. Steps: 1) Go to the benefits portal -> "Manage Dependents" 2) Click "Add Dependent" and upload proof (marriage cert). 3) Select coverage tier for spouse and confirm payroll deduction. 4) If retro coverage is needed (start date earlier than submission), add a comment "retro request" and we will request carrier exception.
payroll-bot: Payroll reminder: If adding a dependent mid-month, premiums are prorated based on benefit carrier billing cycles. Payroll will reflect prorated deduction starting the next payroll run after enrollment confirmation. For example, enroll on 6/10, deduction prorated for June and full for July onward.
harry: FYI from experience: carrier sometimes asks for dependent SSN for enrollment. Have that ready to avoid delays. Also watch for COBRA flags if spouse had COBRA from prior employer.
nina: Good to know. If I request retro coverage back to 6/02 (my hire date), is carrier likely to approve? I had a doctor's visit on 6/05 and would like it covered.
lisa: Retro approvals are on a case-by-case basis. If you submit docs and the medical service occurred within the new-hire window, we submit a retro request. Carrier approvals vary. Please include itemized receipt or EOB when requesting retro review. If carrier denies, we can consider an ad-hoc company reimbursement (processed via Expensify + People Ops) in certain circumstances.
benefits-bot: To file retro reimbursement: upload receipt to Expensify, category `healthcare-reimbursements`, and include description `new-hire dependent retro request`. See template below.

Example Expensify description to copy:
```
Provider: Green Valley Clinic
Date of service: 2026-06-05
Patient: Spouse Name
Service: Primary care visit
Amount: $120.00
Category: healthcare-reimbursements
Notes: New-hire dependent retro request. Enrollment submitted 2026-06-10. Please escalate to benefits admin for carrier review.
```

nina: Thanks  I'll upload the marriage cert + receipt. One more payroll Q  will adding spouse change my pre-tax vs post-tax elections? We have an HSA and I put myself as single contribution.
payroll-bot: When you change coverage tier (single -> family), your HSA contribution limits and FSA elections can be affected. HSA: you can increase contributions up to the family limit pro-rated for the remainder of the year. Make an HSA change request in the benefits portal; payroll will apply pro-rated withholding. FSA: dependent care FSA is a separate election and must be enrolled if you want dependent care pre-tax.
lisa: Also note: if you increase contribution limits mid-year, payroll needs to know if you want to front-load vs evenly spread. If you need an exception, open a ticket and we can coordinate with payroll.
harry: One gotcha  if your spouse is on a plan that required coordination of benefits, claims might route to primary insurer first. That affects how much the carrier will cover retro. Good idea to check spouse's carrier details before the visit.
nina: Uploaded marriage cert and clinic receipt to the benefits portal and submitted Expensify ER-12345 with the template note. Ticket #PO-4550 opened for retro and dependent add. Thanks all! :pray:
lisa: I see PO-4550  I'll route to benefits admin now. Expect a reply within 3 business days about carrier review. If you don't hear back, ping here and I'll escalate.
benefits-bot: PO-4550 confirmed. If carrier approves, payroll will apply any retro premium adjustments and reimbursements as a separate vendor payment. If denied and you requested company reimbursement, payroll will process per policy.
nina: Appreciate it  will follow up if anything else pops up :smile:
